questions.question_text: The opium alkaloids in Papaver somniferum is present as one of the following. Identify.
questions.explanation: Opium alkaloids naturally occur in the plant complexed as salts of meconic acid.

questions.question_text: In expressing vitamin A activity one of the following is true. Identify.

options.A: One RE represents the biological activity in $1 \mu g$ of all trans retinol
options.B: One RE represents the biological activity of $30 \text{ mg}$ of all trans retinol
options.C: One RE represents the biological activity of $0.334 \text{ } \mu \text{g}$ of all trans retinol

questions.explanation: One retinol equivalent (RE) corresponds to $1 \mu \text{g}$ of all-trans-retinol.

questions.question_text: Which of the antineoplastic agent is metabolised by xanthine oxidase?
questions.explanation: Mercaptopurine is inactivated by xanthine oxidase, which is why allopurinol interacts with it.

questions.question_text: The energy of a photon is given by the relationship $E = h\nu$, where

options.A: $E$ is energy of photon in kilo-calories
options.B: $E$ is energy of photon in cycles/sec
options.C: $E$ is the energy of photon in joules
options.D: $E$ is the energy of photon in ergs

questions.explanation: In standard SI units for Planck's relation, energy $E$ is measured in joules.

questions.question_text: Gas chromatographic technique can be used for
questions.explanation: Gas chromatography is widely used for both qualitative identification (via retention time) and quantitative determination.

questions.question_text: Reference compound widely used in NMR spectroscopy for proton spectra in non-aqueous medium is:
questions.explanation: Tetramethylsilane (TMS) is the universal reference standard for $^1\text{H}$ NMR in non-aqueous organic solvents.

questions.question_text: Liposomes are

options.A: Uni or multilayered vesicles of phospholipids

questions.explanation: Liposomes consist of phospholipid bilayers forming spherical vesicles.

questions.question_text: The gonadal hormones like Estrogens, Androgens and Progestins bind with

options.B: Receptors located in the nucleus of the cell
options.C: Receptors located in the contractile vacuoles

questions.explanation: Steroid hormone receptors primarily function as nuclear receptors.

questions.question_text: A highly sensitive semi quantitative method of detecting microbial antigens in biological fluid is:
questions.explanation: Counterimmunoelectrophoresis is commonly employed for rapid detection of microbial antigens.

questions.question_text: Polyene antibiotics such as Amphotericin - B are most likely to

options.D: React with sterols in the membrane

questions.explanation: Amphotericin B binds to ergosterol in fungal cell membranes, creating pores that lead to cell death.

questions.question_text: Among the following statements one of them is most appropriate for $\gamma$ - Interferon. Identify.

options.A: They are virus specific substances and not host specific, naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.B: They are not virus specific substances, however, they are naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.C: They are not virus specific substances, however they are not host specific either. They are naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.D: They are virus specific and host specific naturally occurring glycoproteins.

questions.explanation: Interferons are host-specific, non-virus-specific glycoproteins with antiviral and immunomodulatory activities.

questions.question_text: The tear secretion contains an antibacterial enzyme known as
questions.explanation: Lysozyme is an antimicrobial enzyme found in tears and other bodily secretions.

questions.question_text: A list of ACE inhibition is given below. One of them is not a Prodrug. Identify.
questions.explanation: Captopril is an active drug and does not require ester hydrolysis unlike most other ACE inhibitors.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a pharmacological effect of MORPHINE?
questions.explanation: Morphine causes constipation, not diarrhoea, due to decreased gastrointestinal motility.

questions.question_text: Half life equation for First order reaction is:
questions.explanation: The half-life for a first-order reaction is independent of initial concentration and equals $0.693/K$.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true for alkaloidal bases?

options.A: Water solubility and organic solvent insolubility.
options.B: Water insolubility and organic solvent insolubility.
options.C: Water solubility and organic solvent solubility
options.D: Water insolubility and organic solvent solubility

questions.explanation: Free alkaloidal bases are typically insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

questions.question_text: The conductivity of the solution of an electrolysis is:
questions.explanation: Electrolytic conductivity varies significantly with temperature due to changes in ion mobility and viscosity.

questions.question_text: One of the materials listed below is most commonly used in film coating of tablets. Identify.
questions.explanation: HPMC is the industry standard polymer used for pharmaceutical film coating.

questions.question_text: Lamination is:

options.A: Separation of a tablet into two or more distinct layers
options.B: Partial and complete separation of the top and bottom crowns from the main body of the tablet

questions.explanation: Lamination refers to the separation of a tablet into two or more distinct horizontal layers.

questions.question_text: Among the four OPIOIDS given below one of them is equipotent on $\mu$, $\delta$, $k_1$ and $k_3$ receptor types. Identify.
questions.explanation: Morphine acts across various opioid receptor subtypes.

questions.question_text: An amperometric titrations which one of the following is kept constant?
questions.explanation: In amperometry, a constant potential is applied to the indicator electrode while measuring current.

questions.question_text: Disposable syringes are made up of
questions.explanation: Polypropylene is widely used for manufacturing medical-grade disposable syringes.

questions.question_text: Typhoid vaccine IP is a sterile suspension or a freeze dried solid prepared from
questions.explanation: Typhoid vaccines are prepared from killed or attenuated Salmonella typhi.

questions.question_text: In the microbiological assay of bacitracin \ce{IP} the test organism used is
questions.explanation: Micrococcus luteus is typically used as the test organism for bacitracin microbiological assays.

questions.question_text: In the general formula \ce{R-X-C-C-N}: $X = \text{Nitrogen}$, or $\text{Carbon}$, $R = \text{Different groups}$. This formula represents
questions.explanation: Ethanolamine-type antihistamines follow this core aminoalkyl ether/amine structural framework.

questions.question_text: The biological source of cinnamon bark is:

options.A: Dried inner bark of the shoot of coppiced trees of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Family - Lauraceae
options.B: Dried inner bark of the shoot of coppiced trees of Cinnamomum indicum Family - Lauraceae
options.C: Dried wood bark of Cinnamomum Camphora Family - Lauraceae
options.D: Dried inner bark of the shoot of coppiced trees of Cinnamomum loureirii Family - Lauraceae

questions.explanation: Cinnamon consists of the dried inner bark of the shoots of coppiced trees of Cinnamomum zeylanicum.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct geneva name for CORTISONE.
questions.explanation: Cortisone IUPAC nomenclature defines it as a pregnene derivative with keto groups at C3, C11, and C20 and hydroxyls at C17 and C21.

questions.question_text: Identify one of the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that inhibit only luminal carbonic anhydrase enzyme?
questions.explanation: Benzolamide is a positively charged carbonic anhydrase inhibitor targeted to luminal/extracellular enzymes.

questions.question_text: Testosterone is rapidly converted to one of the following metabolic products in many tissues, which is the active androgen?
questions.explanation: Testosterone is converted by 5-alpha-reductase into $5\alpha$-dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the more potent active androgen.

questions.question_text: One of the following drugs is an alkylating agent. Identify.
questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is a nitrogen mustard alkylating antineoplastic agent.

questions.question_text: Listed below are structures of sulphonamides. Which one of them is used as an anti-diabetic drug?
questions.explanation: Sulfonylurea structures like tolbutamide derivatives contain the characteristic sulfonylurea bridge used for anti-diabetic activity.

questions.question_text: Four sets of intermediates are listed below. Choose the correct set for the synthesis of BUPIVACAINE IP.
questions.explanation: Bupivacaine is synthesized from pipecolic acid chloride (or $\alpha$-picolinic acid derivative) and 2,6-diethylaniline.

questions.question_text: Among the immunizing agents listed below one of them is orally administered. Identify.
questions.explanation: Sabin polio vaccine (OPV) is administered orally.

questions.question_text: In vitro dissolution rate studies on drug product are useful in bioavailability evaluations if they are correlated with

options.B: In-vivo studies in at least thee species of animals
options.C: The chemical stability of the drug

questions.explanation: In vitro dissolution must be correlated with in vivo human bioavailability data (IVIVC).

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of antiviral drugs is given. Match with closely associated drugs given in (A) to (D). (1) Inhibit an early step in viral replication viral uni-coating (2) Irreversible inactivation of DNA Polymerase
questions.explanation: Amantadine inhibits viral uncoating (1-A) and Acyclovir targets DNA polymerase (2-D).

questions.question_text: Given below are the etiologic agents. Match with common name of the infection listed in (A) to (D): (1) Enterobius vermicularis (2) Taenia saginata
questions.explanation: Enterobius vermicularis causes pinworm (1-B) and Taenia saginata is a tapeworm (2-A/C).

questions.question_text: The substance mentioned below elicit the therapeutic effect given in (A) to (D): (1) Hepatitis B. Immuno globulin antibodies (2) Tetanus Toxoid
questions.explanation: Hepatitis B immune globulin provides passive transfer of antibodies (1-C), while tetanus toxoid induces active immunity (2-A).

questions.question_text: The following glycosides of Digitalis Purpurea give on hydrolysis the genius and sugars listed in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Purpurea Glycoside-A (2) Purpurea Glycoside-B
questions.explanation: Glycoside A and B hydrolysis products correspond to specific cardenolide aglycones coupled with glucose and digitoxose units.

questions.question_text: Listed are some important antibiotics (A) to (D). match them. (1) Bacitracin (2) Erythromycin
questions.explanation: Bacitracin is a peptide antibiotic from amino acids, whereas erythromycin is a macrolide built from propionate units.

questions.question_text: The substitution of R in \ce{R-CO-NH-CH-CH} is listed in A to D for the following antibiotics. Match Them: (1) CLOXACILLIN (2) CARBENICILLIN
questions.explanation: Cloxacillin corresponds to the isoxazolyl penicillin structure (A), and carbenicillin contains the phenyl-malonic acid side chain (B).

questions.question_text: Some of the vitamins listed below are associated with co-enzyme given in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Nicotinic Acid (2) Riboflavin
questions.explanation: Nicotinic acid forms Coenzyme I (NAD+) and Riboflavin forms FAD.

questions.question_text: Listed are some tablets additives. Match them with their correct use given in (A) to (D). (1) Acacia (2) Lactose
questions.explanation: Acacia is commonly used as a tablet binder, and lactose is widely used as a diluent.

questions.question_text: The compounds listed are assayed by method given (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Pyridoxine Hydrochloride I.P (2) Ranitidine Hydrochloride
questions.explanation: Pyridoxine hydrochloride and many basic amine hydrochlorides are commonly assayed by non-aqueous titration.

questions.question_text: The following techniques are associated with the support materials used in the column which are given in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Size exclusion chromatography (2) H P L C

options.A: Octadecyl silane chemically bounded to Porous silica

questions.explanation: HPLC typically uses octadecyl silane (ODS) bonded to porous silica (C18 columns).

questions.question_text: For the following potentiometric titrations indicator electrode used is given from (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Acid base (2) Complexometry
questions.explanation: Glass electrode is the primary indicator electrode for acid-base potentiometric titrations.

questions.question_text: Following ring systems are present in the alkaloids listed (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Imidazole (2) Isoquinoline
questions.explanation: Pilocarpine contains an imidazole ring, and Papaverine contains an isoquinoline ring system.

questions.question_text: Following constituents are present in drugs listed in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) D-Linalool (2) Panaxadiol
questions.explanation: D-Linalool is a major constituent of Coriandrum sativum, and Panaxadiol is found in Ginseng.

questions.question_text: Systematic name of the following biologically important purines are given in (A) to (D). Match them correctly. (1) Adenine (2) Guanine
questions.explanation: Adenine is systematically 6-aminopurine, and guanine is 2-amino-6-oxypurine.

questions.question_text: The drugs mentioned below are synthesized from intermediates listed in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Meprobamate (2) Diazepam
questions.explanation: Diazepam is synthesized from 2-amino-5-chlorobenzophenone and ethyl glycinate.

questions.question_text: Some of the drugs listed below from (A) to (D) are having specific mechanism of action. Match them. (1) Interferes with the renin-angiotensin system (2) Directly relaxes arteriolar smooth muscles and thus decreases peripheral resistance
questions.explanation: Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor that interferes with the renin-angiotensin system, while hydralazine directly relaxes arteriolar smooth muscle.

questions.question_text: Given below from (A) to (D) are application forms for the specific purpose listed as per (D) and (C) Act. Match them. (1) Manufacture of cosmetics (2) Retail sale of schedule C and C1 drugs
questions.explanation: Form 31 is typically associated with cosmetics manufacture and Form 20C/21 for specific sales under drug regulations.

questions.question_text: For many drugs in the I.P. exact solubility limits are not listed. Instead, descriptive terminology is employed. Match the numbered solubility limits with the correct lettered solubility expression (gm/ml). (1) Very soluble (2) Sparingly soluble
questions.explanation: Very soluble corresponds to less than 1 part solvent per part solute, and sparingly soluble is from 30 to 100 parts.

questions.question_text: It is often desirable to formulate a dosage form so that its pH is approximately equivalent to that of the area of which it is administered. Match them. (1) Blood (2) Skin
questions.explanation: Normal blood pH is approximately 7.4, and the skin surface pH is typically acidic around 5.5.

questions.question_text: The following microscopical characteristic is associated with the drugs mentioned in (A) to (D). Match them. (1) Rubiaceous type of stomata (Paracytic) (2) Ranunculaceous type of stomata
questions.explanation: Rubiaceous stomata are found in drugs like Ipecac or certain leaves, while ranunculaceous (anomocytic) stomata are characteristic of digitalis and other dicot leaves.
